title: Abu Bakr, as-Siddiq
hookLine: Abu Bakr believes without hesitation and brings others: Uthman, Talhah, Zubayr, Abd al-Rahman, Sa'd

cards: Some answers take weeks. Others come before the question is finished.
In Ibn Ishaq's sirah, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is remembered as saying that everyone he invited to Islam hesitated, held back, thought it over, except one man.

When he told Abu Bakr, Abu Bakr did not hold back and did not hesitate. A merchant of Quraysh, well known and well liked, a man people came to with their business and their questions. He hears it, and says yes.

teach.b: His title is as-Siddiq. Tradition explains it through sidq, truthfulness: a siddiq is someone who confirms the truth, who takes a true word as true.

There's a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, from a later quarrel among the companions, where the Prophet defends him with a memory: when he was sent, people said, you are lying, and Abu Bakr said, he has spoken the truth, and stood by him with himself and his wealth.
That is what the name holds.

Sirah writers also tell that the title stuck after the Night Journey, when Abu Bakr was told the Prophet claimed to have gone to Jerusalem and back in a night, and answered that if he said it, it was true.
That story belongs later in the year. Abu Bakr didn't keep his yes to himself.

Ibn Ishaq names the men who came to Islam through him: Uthman ibn Affan, az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, names that will come back again and again.
He brought them to the Prophet, and they believed. How? Ibn Ishaq describes him as a man people liked to sit with, who knew the genealogies of Quraysh, easy and kind in company.
His friends trusted him, so they listened.
The same quality that made him believe at once made others willing to hear.

how: Sunni Muslims know Abu Bakr as as-Siddiq, say 'may Allah be pleased with him' after his name, and honor him as the first caliph; Shia Muslims read the succession after the Prophet differently. His early belief is retold in sirah study.

the young cousin who grew up in his house

games.q: you're Abu Bakr. your friend tells you something has come to him from Allah in a cave. what do you do?
o: wait to see what others say.
games.why: Ibn Ishaq remembers him as the one who did not hesitate, and then he brought his own friends.

practice: Think of one good thing that has helped you, a class, a walk, a habit, a place of worship, a book, and one friend who trusts you and might be glad of it.
Picture telling them simply, without pressure; if you pray, ask for that friend's good.

wordCard.voice: Abu Bakr. The friend who said yes without hesitating, called as-Siddiq, the one who confirms the truth, and who brought others with him. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: one who confirms the truth; tradition links it to sidq, truthfulness.

carryVoice: Your line: he believed at once. His friends listened because they trusted him. Day seven hundred twenty-nine, done.
